measurement_source.notes: One recorded serial run; elapsed time includes transfer and extraction/checkout. TSV on_disk_bytes and archive_compressed_bytes are du -sk allocations rounded to 1 KiB. Checkout metrics were independently recomputed from retained worktrees with lstat: regular-file bytes and symlink path bytes are distinguished; allocation is st_blocks*512.
measurement_source.archive_file: codex.tar.gz in benchmark workspace; size and integrity verified 2026-10-13

methods.archive_integrity: tar -tzf succeeded; 9017 regular file entries, all bytes matched retained extracted tree

methods.source: depth-1, single-branch clone, pinned tag rust-v0.162.1
depth-1, blob:none, sparse paths docs and codex-rs/core, pinned tag rust-v0.162.1

limitations: Network bytes were not captured by an independent interface or process monitor. Archive size is the local compressed response file; Git metadata/pack size is not a wire-transfer measurement.
All cases ran serially in a shared environment; proxy, DNS, GitHub CDN, and OS cache state may affect elapsed times. The numbers are one observation, not a stable performance guarantee.
Sparse checkout has intentionally incomplete worktree content. It is not a full source mirror and Git may fetch promised blobs later when requested.
GitHub's annotated tag reference object SHA differs from the peeled commit checked out; the benchmark checkout resolves to 092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d.
Archive compressed byte length is confirmed from the retained codex.tar.gz (17,186,781 bytes); its tar listing and integrity test passed, and every regular file matched the retained extracted tree.
Checkout logical bytes count regular-file payloads and report symlink path bytes separately; this avoids counting symlink target contents as if they were duplicated in the archive.
